issues.failure_explanation: Finite first moments of X and Y do not imply that XY is integrable, so either side of the asserted identity can be undefined. For example, taking X=Y with finite first moment but infinite second moment satisfies the stated hypothesis while E(XY) is not finite.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis E|XY|<infinity, or state another standard sufficient integrability condition.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem4 is false as stated. Its particular later application involves finite discrete sampling and can be bypassed directly, so the subsequent results are not necessarily invalidated by this defect.
issues.title: Insufficient integrability hypothesis for conditional-expectation identity
issues.why_classification: A single standard local hypothesis repairs the lemma without changing any substantive convergence claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions allow zero rows to receive positive sampling probability. For example, with q=1 and a nonzero matrix having one zero row, Definition def:batchSampling can assign positive probability to every row, but sampling the zero row gives S_tau A_tau=0. The displayed division is then by zero, the corresponding beta entry can be zero, and B_{S;i}^{-1} is undefined. Nonzeroness of A as a whole does not imply nonzeroness of every sampled block.

failure_location.quote:
Let $A\in\reals^{m\times n}$ be a
  nonzero matrix, $r\in\range(A)$ be a nonzero vector, and $S\in\mathbb{DR}^{m\times m}$ be a nonsingular diagonal matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every block in the support of the sampling to contain a nonzero row, or separately handle zero sampled blocks and redefine the corresponding diagonal-bound entries so that no division by zero occurs.
issues.overall_effect: The principal bound and the sharper theorem are not defined for all matrices and samplings allowed by their statements; the relaxed corollary's supplied proof also passes through this unsupported lemma.
issues.title: Lemma 6 permits sampled zero matrices and undefined inverse bounds
issues.why_classification: Excluding or separately treating redundant zero equations is a local degenerate-case repair that leaves the method and rates for substantive systems unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses permit d_tau=d. Then W_tau has zero columns and W_tau^T A^T D^2 A W_tau is a 0-by-0 matrix, which has no positive eigenvalue under the paper's definition of lambda_min. Thus xi_tau and every rate taking a minimum over such blocks are undefined. The one-row system A=[1] with q=1 is already an allowed example.

failure_location.quote:
Let the columns of matrices  $V_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times d_{\tau}}$ and $W_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times (d-d_{\tau})}$
  be the orthonormal bases of the subspaces $\range(A_{\tau}^{\T})$ and $\mathcal{W}_{\tau}$, respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the case d_tau=d and use the fact that the preceding projection has already produced the least-norm solution, or introduce and justify an explicit convention yielding a valid contraction factor for this case.
issues.overall_effect: All post-first-iteration rate formulas fail to cover samplings containing a block that already spans range(A^T), despite such samplings being allowed and potentially solving the system exactly.
issues.title: Complement-space rate is undefined when a sampled block spans the row space
issues.why_classification: The missing case has an immediate exact-convergence argument, so a short local case split can preserve all substantive guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: For row pavings with unequal block sizes, the framework pads a smaller block by repeating indices. The spectral norm in Lemma lem6 is that of the repeated-row matrix S_tau A_tau, not the effective-set matrix S_T A_T. In the paper's own singleton example, tau=(1,1), so ||S_tau A_tau||_2^2=2|s_1|^2||A^{(1)}||_2^2, whereas ||S_{T_1}A_{T_1}||_2^2=|s_1|^2||A^{(1)}||_2^2. Hence the asserted equality and the resulting B_S are false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the theorem to equal-sized paving blocks sampled without repetition, or redefine B_S using the maximum repeated-row norm over all tuple representations and redo the resulting rate formula.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate row-paving rate can underestimate the relevant block norms and is unsupported for the advertised general row paving with unequal block sizes.
issues.title: Row-paving simplification ignores repeated rows used to pad unequal blocks
issues.why_classification: A repair is contained, but it either removes the general unequal-block regime or materially changes and potentially weakens the advertised bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem5 would yield the displayed inequality only from nonnegative covariance between xi and the squared error norm, not between xi and the norm. These signs need not agree. For sample norm values (0,1,3) and xi values (1,10,4), the covariance of xi with the norm is positive, while the covariance with its square is negative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the assumption by nonnegative sample covariance between xi and ||x^(k)-x_star||_2^2, or supply a new argument deriving that stronger relation from valid hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The key empirical factorization used to obtain the proposed sharper rate is invalid under the theorem's stated covariance assumption.
issues.title: Covariance assumption does not justify the squared-error product inequality
issues.why_classification: The inference can be repaired locally only by imposing a materially stronger correlation condition; the theorem remains recognizable but applies under a different substantive hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which holds with probability at least $1-\delta$.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation thm4Eq8 is an inequality between random empirical averages that holds only on a high-probability event. Taking unconditional expectation does not preserve that inequality: the failure event contributes uncontrolled terms. Moreover, thm4Eq2 contains only population expectations and is deterministic, so describing it as holding with probability at least 1-delta does not follow from the empirical Hoeffding event. The random sample-covariance condition is also imposed on the same samples without controlling the probability of its intersection with that event.

failure_location.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish an appropriate population correlation relation and control the failure event, or else restate the conclusion purely as an empirical high-probability bound rather than an expected convergence rate.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's concentration-based expected convergence-rate theorem, its claimed sharper theoretical bound, and the experimental comparisons using that bound lack a valid population-level guarantee.
issues.title: High-probability empirical inequality is converted invalidly into a population MSE bound
issues.why_classification: Repairing the empirical-to-population passage requires new probabilistic architecture, while the immediate alternative changes the central guarantee from a population MSE rate to a finite-sample empirical statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we construct ill-conditioned matrices by modifying a row block of the data matrix $A$ so that some singular values are significantly smaller than the larger ones.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula does not ensure that the asserted entries are nonzero or valid nonnegative singular values. For sufficiently large i it becomes negative, and it is exactly zero whenever beta sigma_min(A)=(i-1)ell. Negative diagonal entries produce singular values equal to their absolute values, which need not be decreasing and need not have the claimed small-value structure.

failure_location.quote: Construct a diagonal matrix $\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{q \times n}$ with decreasing nonzero diagonal entries defined by $\sigma_i = \beta \sigma_{\min}(A) - (i-1)\ell$, where the scaling factor is $\beta=0.2$ and the decrement is $\ell=0.01$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the arithmetic sequence by an explicitly positive decreasing sequence, with parameters chosen relative to q and sigma_min(A), and regenerate or revalidate the affected experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The described experimental generator does not guarantee the advertised ill-conditioned matrices, so the interpretation of the corresponding numerical tests is unreliable as written.
issues.title: Ill-conditioned test construction does not define valid prescribed singular values
issues.why_classification: The construction can be replaced locally, but doing so requires regenerating and rechecking an entire advertised family of numerical experiments.
